subject: Vocabulary
description: Latin roots VID/VIS (see) — visible, vision, evidence, video, supervise, provide, revise, advice, evident.

questions.stem: The root VID/VIS means 'to see'. EVIDENCE literally means:

options.option_text: What can be seen as proof
What is heard about a case

questions.explanation: EVIDENCE — etymology e (out) + vid (see) → 'WHAT IS SEEN OUTWARDLY' → that which is APPARENT, observable, can serve as proof. WORD FAMILY (root VID/VIS = see): (1) VISIBLE — capable of being seen. (2) INVISIBLE — not capable of being seen. (3) VISION — sight, ability to see. (4) VIEW — what is seen. (5) VIDEO — Latin 'I see' (video = first-person singular). (6) SUPERVISE (super + vise) — to oversee. (7) ADVISE (ad + vise) — to give counsel ('look toward'). (8) ENVISION — to see in mind. (9) PROVIDE (pro + vid) — to see ahead, anticipate. (10) PRUDENT — see before, careful (from pro + vidence). (11) REVISE (re + vis) — to look at again. (12) PROVIDENCE — divine foresight. (13) EVIDENT — visible, obvious. (14) PROVIDENT — having foresight. (15) SURVEY (sur + vid) — to look over (from French). EXAMPLES: 'visual', 'vista', 'vis-à-vis' (face-to-face). MEDICAL: 'amblyopia' (lazy eye); 'myopia' (near-sightedness). PYQ FREQUENCY: VID/VIS root vocab in SSC CGL, CAT, IBPS PO English — top common-root MCQ ~2 per paper.

questions.stem: What does PROVIDENT mean (root VID = see + PRO = forward)?
questions.explanation: PROVIDENT — adjective: showing FORESIGHT, careful PLANNING for the future. ETYMOLOGY: pro (forward) + vid (see) = 'seeing ahead'. EXAMPLES: 'a provident person who saves for retirement'; 'her provident habits ensured the family had savings during the recession'. SYNONYMS: prudent, far-sighted, thrifty, frugal, judicious. ANTONYMS: improvident, reckless, spendthrift, profligate, wasteful. INDIA CONTEXT — EMPLOYEES' PROVIDENT FUND (EPF, 1952): mandatory retirement savings scheme; managed by EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund Organisation) under Ministry of Labour. EPF rate (2024-25): 8.25% on contributions. RELATED: PPF (Public Provident Fund) — 15-year voluntary savings scheme. THE CONCEPT: 'providence' = divine foresight; 'providential' = lucky, as if guided by foresight ('a providential escape'). DON'T CONFUSE: 'PROVIDENT' (forward-looking) vs 'PROVINCIAL' (relating to a province; narrow-minded; from 'province'). EXAM-FAVOURITE: synonym/antonym Qs around 'provident' often use 'prudent' or 'reckless' as test answers. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'provident' in SSC CGL, CAT 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: REVISION, from VIS root, literally means:
questions.explanation: REVISION — etymology re (again) + vis (see) = 'TO SEE/LOOK AGAIN'. Original meaning: re-examining text/ideas to refine, correct, improve. CONTEXTS: (1) STUDENT REVISION — re-reading material to reinforce learning. (2) MANUSCRIPT REVISION — author edits draft. (3) HISTORIOGRAPHY — 'historical revisionism' = re-examining accepted historical narratives (sometimes pejorative if disputing well-established facts). (4) STATISTICAL REVISION — updating GDP/inflation figures. (5) CONSTITUTIONAL REVISION — formal constitutional amendment. WORD FAMILY: REVISE (verb), REVISION (noun), REVISIONIST (one who revises). DON'T CONFUSE: REVISION (looking again) vs REVISIT (going again to a place); REVIEW (formal evaluation, often by others); RECAP (informal summary). EXAM TIP: students often equate 'revision' with 'memorizing' — but it's literally 'seeing again', which IS a form of mental review. STUDY ADVICE: spaced REVISION (spaced repetition) is the most evidence-backed memory technique — used by Anki app, Duolingo, etc. PYQ FREQUENCY: VIS-root vocab in SSC CGL, CAT 2 per paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: rewards systematic root-knowledge.

questions.explanation: ENVISAGE — verb meaning 'to IMAGINE, FORESEE, picture in mind'. ETYMOLOGY: en (in) + visage (face — French for face, from VIS/VID 'see'). Literally 'to face up to' or 'to confront in vision'. SAMPLE USAGES: 'I can envisage the project being completed by next year.' 'The architects envisaged a building blending into the natural landscape.' SYNONYMS: envision, imagine, foresee, picture, visualize, anticipate, contemplate. RELATED WORDS: VISAGE = the face, especially as an indicator of mood or character ('a stern visage'). VISTA = a long view through a passage; mental view of future. NUANCE: 'envisage' often implies a CONSIDERED MENTAL PICTURE of something planned for the future — slightly more formal than 'imagine'. CONTEXTS: business plans, architectural designs, political reform discussions. EXAM TRAP: students confuse 'envisage' with 'envy' (jealousy) or 'envious' (jealous) — completely different roots (envy from Latin 'invidere' = to look askance). ALSO: 'face/face' — visage and 'physiognomy' (face-reading) are related concepts. PYQ FREQUENCY: ENVISAGE in CAT, GRE, advanced UPSC essay grading; SSC CGL Tier 2 vocabulary 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: VISIONARY (from VIS root) means a person who:
questions.explanation: VISIONARY — noun/adjective: a person with original, IMAGINATIVE thoughts about the future; or having visions/dreams. Both meanings stem from 'seeing beyond the present'. EXAMPLES: 'Steve Jobs was a visionary entrepreneur.' 'The visionary architect designed a city for 2050.' SYNONYMS (positive): innovator, pioneer, futurist, dreamer (positive sense), prophet (in business/political context). NEGATIVE CONNOTATION possible: a 'visionary' can mean impractical dreamer ('His ideas are visionary but not implementable'). SAMPLE INDIAN VISIONARIES: A.P.J. ABDUL KALAM (Vision 2020), MAHATMA GANDHI (non-violent independence), J.R.D. TATA (industrial India), VIKRAM SARABHAI (space program), VERGHESE KURIEN (White Revolution, Amul founder). RELATED: VISION STATEMENTS (corporate) — describing where an organization aspires to go in 5-10 years. EXAM CONTEXT — UPSC ESSAY: 'visionary leadership' is a frequent essay-prompt theme. PYQ FREQUENCY: VISIONARY appears in SSC CGL synonyms-section, CAT vocab, UPSC essay 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: rewards depth of vocabulary linked to leadership/strategy concepts.

questions.explanation: SUPERVISION — etymology super (above, over) + vis (see) = 'LOOKING OVER'. NOUN: the act of overseeing, monitoring, directing. PARALLEL FORMS: SUPERVISE (verb), SUPERVISOR (noun for the person), SUPERVISORY (adjective). SUPERVISION is core to many domains: (1) WORKPLACE — supervisor manages team. (2) ACADEMIC — PhD supervisor guides research. (3) CHILDCARE — adult supervision required. (4) FINANCIAL — RBI supervises banks; SEBI supervises securities markets. (5) MEDICAL — doctor supervises trainees. ETYMOLOGY DEEP-DIVE: 'super' = above, beyond (also gives super-natural, super-power, super-vise, supersonic). 'vis' = see. So 'supervisor' = 'one who sees from above' — captures the bird's-eye-view metaphor of management. RELATED OVERSIGHT WORDS: AUDIT (ear-related, hear), INSPECT (in + spec, look into), MONITOR (to warn), OVERSIGHT (literal English compound). CIVIL SERVICES: 'supervisory cadre' includes IAS, IPS, IRS officers. PYQ FREQUENCY: SUPERVISION-related vocab in SSC CGL synonyms, CAT 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests root-meaning under standard English word.

questions.stem: What does INVIDIOUS mean (related to the root VID 'see')?

options.option_text: Likely to cause envy or resentment
Having the inability to see well

questions.explanation: INVIDIOUS — adjective: likely to AROUSE RESENTMENT or ANGER in others; UNFAIRLY DISCRIMINATING; tending to give offense. ETYMOLOGY: in (against) + vid (see) → 'looking at WITH ENVY' — old Latin 'invidiosus' = envious, hateful. Same root spawns the word ENVY. SAMPLE USAGES: 'It would be invidious to single out one student over another for praise.' 'The judge faced the invidious task of choosing between two equally talented finalists.' 'invidious comparisons' = unfair, resentment-causing comparisons. SYNONYMS: discriminatory, unjust, unfair, offensive, odious, repugnant, distasteful. ANTONYMS: equitable, fair, impartial. KEY DISTINCTION: INVIDIOUS (causing offense/envy) vs INSIDIOUS (treacherous, gradually harmful) — students often confuse these two. INSIDIOUS = sneaky, gradual, like a hidden disease (e.g., 'insidious effects of smoking'). DON'T CONFUSE: ENVIOUS (jealous of others) is the FEELING; INVIDIOUS describes situations or actions that PROVOKE that feeling. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'invidious' is a top CAT, GRE-tier vocab MCQ; less common in SSC. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests advanced English vocabulary distinctions.
